Onboarding & first-routine flow

Every screen ("book") from Karen's wireframes and dictation, in journey order. Click any screen to see its chapters — the conditional copy and button targets that drive it. Source of truth for engineering is the git-tracked Screens/*.md files this page is built from; this page is the walkthrough layer.

Drafted — chapters + JSON ready Mockup only — no copy written Not specified — no mockup, no copy External — not part of this spec

Global goals

what every screen below is being checked against
01

Close the leaderboard dead-end

Explored-leaderboard users should be actively routed to Home, not stranded there.

02

Guest → account conversion

Meaningfully increase guest sign-ups, not just tolerate guests passing through.

03

Free → Pro conversion

The paywall is a deliberate conversion moment, not incidental placement.

04

Drip education actually lands

The gated education sequence should get seen and completed, not just be technically gate-able.

Numeric targets intentionally TBD — qualitative goals locked 2026-08-19.

  RT2 -- locked type tapped, free --> PAY[Paywall]

Returning users — First Screen

click a cell to open that chapter

Guest gets 2 buttons throughout (Full Body / Customize). Free gets a 3rd ("Last routine settings") from routine 1 onward, and a countdown message from routine 3 as the trial pool depletes.

Routine Type 2 — routine 7+ entry & the free-tier lock

From routine 7, free users land here directly instead of the wizard. Only Full Body is tappable — everything else is visible but locked.

Trial & paywall model

measured in completed routines, not calendar days
Routine 0Guest: 7-routine pool starts
Routine 7Free: +7 added to whatever's left (typical total: 14)
Routine 8Soft paywall appears
Routine 14Hard paywall — last unlocked routine

A guest who passes routine 7 without signing up gets the same gating as a budget-exhausted free user: Full Body only, other types blurred, tap → paywall.

The day-5/routine-5 "60 days for $2 + bonus coins + streak tokens" offer and the Routine Type 2 lock banner's share offer are the same promotion. Shown plain first; the share-with-a-friend version is introduced later, not bundled with the first appearance.
